text:
Step-1  Form the 1,3-dithiolane  
Propanal (CH3–CH2–CHO) + 1,2-ethanedithiol (EDT) / BF3 → cyclic thio-acetal A  
         (Et)–CH–(S–CH2–CH2–S)        (Et = CH3CH2)

Step-2  Deprotonate and alkylate  
A  +  BuLi  → lithio-dithiolane B  
B  +  EtBr  → alkylated dithiolane C  
         (Et)–C(Et)–(S–CH2–CH2–S)

Step-3  Remove the protecting group  
C  +  HgCl2 / H2O / H+  → ketone D  
         (Et)2C=O   (3-pentanone, i.e. diethyl ketone)

Step-4  Prepare a Wittig ylide and react  
Ph3P + 3-bromopentane → phosphonium salt → BuLi → ylide  
          (Et)2C= PPh3⁺Br⁻  →  (Et)2C⁻–PPh3⁺

Wittig reaction of this ylide with ketone D gives the alkene

E : (Et)2C = C(Et)2
     i.e. the double bond joins two identical carbon centres, each bearing two ethyl
     groups.

Step-5  Count the distinct 13C environments in E  

Because the molecule is highly symmetrical:

1. The two sp2 carbons of the C=C bond are equivalent → 1 signal.  
2. Each ethyl group is attached in the same way; all four α-CH2 carbons are equivalent → 1 signal.  
3. All four terminal CH3 carbons are equivalent → 1 signal.

Total distinct 13C-NMR signals = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

Answer: C
